title: Minimum Window Substring
description: Given strings `s` and `t`, return the shortest substring of `s` that contains every character of `t`, counting multiplicity (if `t` has two `a`s, the window needs at least two). If no such window exists, return the empty string `""`. The answer is guaranteed to be unique when it exists.

examples.explanation: It is the shortest window holding X, Y and Z.

constraints: s and t consist of English letters (case-sensitive).
hints: Checking every substring against t is far too slow. Count how many of each letter t requires.
Grow a window on the right until it satisfies every requirement, then try to shrink it from the left while it stays satisfied.
Track how many distinct letters currently meet their required count. When that equals the number of distinct letters in t, record the window and move left.

class Solution:

solution.explanation: Count the letters t needs. Move the right pointer, decrementing the need for each letter, and count how many distinct letters are fully satisfied. Once all are satisfied, record the window and advance left, re-adding needs as letters leave, until the window becomes invalid again. Each pointer moves at most n times, so time is O(n + m) with O(m) space for the counts.
